items.body: The new deadline and memory sampler stop when conversion returns. Metadata extraction, structure/link extraction, chunking and persistence then execute without either budget. Native files and compiled executables bypass enforcement entirely. R2 explicitly requires bounded conversion and post-conversion processing; replacing one quadratic parser does not enforce that contract.
items.suggestion: Extend enforceable time/memory limits through per-file processing, recording the budget error and continuing with subsequent files. Cover post-conversion overruns in regression tests.
items.title: The new deadline and memory sampler stop when conversion returns

items.body: Post-conversion limits are checked only after synchronous phases return. They detect an overrun but cannot bound it or prevent memory exhaustion during that phase. Reproduced using the current code-region parser and file-budget implementation: a 40,000-row Markdown table ran 3,984 ms against a 1,000 ms budget; the slow-file timer could not fire. The new slow-chunker test likewise verifies eventual error recording, not interruption. Finding #1 is improved but remains unresolved.
items.suggestion: Execute potentially unbounded processing in a terminable worker, or introduce bounded processing increments with deadline/memory checks. Test that processing stops near its configured deadline and subsequent files continue.
items.title: Post-conversion limits are checked only after synchronous phases return

items.body: `scanFencedCodeRanges(markdown)` scans frontmatter and HTML comments before respecting their excluded ranges. A fence inside either can open a code block extending through the remaining document, silently dropping real links. Reproduced with a YAML block scalar containing an indented triple-backtick line: `[[real-link]]` disappears when padding pushes the note over the parser threshold. The parser path preserves it.
items.suggestion: Prevent excluded frontmatter/comment content from opening fences; add threshold-crossing regression tests.
items.title: `scanFencedCodeRanges(markdown)` scans frontmatter and HTML comments before respecting their excluded ranges

items.body:
Inline delimiters pair globally across paragraph boundaries. For `A stray \` character.

[[real-link]]

Another \` character.`, the fallback hides the real link, whereas the parser correctly finds no code span. The scanner also discards backslash-preceded closing backticks, although backslashes do not escape delimiters inside code spans; this can extend exclusions across subsequent links. Both failures reproduced.
items.suggestion: Bound pairing to valid inline contexts and distinguish opener escaping from closing-delimiter rules.
items.title: Inline delimiters pair globally across paragraph boundaries

items.body: The fallback does not recognize fences inside blockquotes. Reproduced with `> ~~~\n> [[example-only]]\n> ~~~`: adding padding to cross the parser threshold causes `example-only` to become an indexed link. This changes graph contents solely because the note grows.
items.suggestion: Track container prefixes when recognizing fenced blocks and test quoted/list-contained fences on the fallback path.
items.title: The fallback does not recognize fences inside blockquotes
